daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo met with a drafting team to advance the One Data Indonesia Law, signaling a push to consolidate national data governance. The meeting represents an effort to establish unified data standards across government agencies. This legislative initiative is part of broader administrative reforms under the new administration.

  • Former President Jokowi is reportedly headed toward becoming PSI party chairman amid unclear coalition dynamics, marking his return to formal partisan politics after leaving the presidency.
  • Vice President Gibran stated he is not angry at the plaintiff who challenged his educational equivalency certificate at the State Administrative Court, even as his legal team prepares evidence and the plaintiff withdraws the suit.
  • Indonesia's Electoral Law remains unsigned ahead of the 2029 elections, raising questions about preparedness for the upcoming electoral cycle.
  • The Presidential Advisory Council (Wantimpres) is finalizing its first recommendations for President Prabowo across three sectoral areas.
  • A DPR member called for maximum criminal penalties for corporations suspected in forest fires and demanded their profits be seized.
  • The head of the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) clarified that a Rp 1 trillion incentive from the Home Ministry is not exclusively designated for the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program.
  • National Police Chief partnered with Muhammadiyah to prevent online gambling through education in schools and Islamic boarding schools.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia called for ASEAN-Japan cooperation to combat cyber threats, pushing for enhanced regional legal frameworks to address cross-border digital crime. The initiative reflects Indonesia's continued advocacy for stronger multilateral coordination on cybersecurity challenges. Indonesian officials emphasized the growing sophistication of cyber threats facing Southeast Asia.

  • Indonesian Marines captured the commander and deputy of the OPM Aikum Battalion in Maybrat during Operation Badai Kasuari 3.13.
  • Indonesian troops uncovered a weapons cache belonging to an armed group in Papua.
  • An Indonesian Navy ship conducted gun drills in the Bali Sea as part of routine training operations.
  • Defence Minister Sjafrie asked TNI soldiers to prepare for forest fire threats, while reminding troops in Pacitan to honor the legacies of General Soedirman and former President SBY.
  • Baznas announced it will add 300 scholarships in the Middle East, with Palestinian students receiving particular attention.

Other

Indonesia's composite stock index (IHSG) fell to 4,990, continuing a sharp decline that saw the index drop 2.6 percent during the first trading session. Bank Indonesia responded to concerns over potential rupiah weakness, stating that the impact from an MSCI proposal would be short-lived, though analysts warned the currency could weaken to Rp 21,000 per US dollar.

  • President Prabowo will inaugurate the CATL-Antam battery plant, marking a major milestone in Indonesia's downstream battery industry development.
  • The government reported that its MSME credit scheme has supported 12 million jobs as of October, demonstrating the program's employment impact.
  • State logistics agency Bulog absorbed 4.25 million tons of rice, exceeding its procurement target by 106 percent.
  • The BGN head said the agency is targeting 5,000 to 10,000 feeding centers to serve buffet-style meals under the MBG program, with plans to connect 10,000 centers via CCTV to strengthen monitoring.
  • The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) conducted searches in Kudus involving cigarette manufacturer PT Djarum, prompting a response from the Directorate General of Customs and Excise.
